Stage 5 · Grammar

Grammar

The Past Simple — irregular verbs.
Track 7.3 — irregular verbs in sound groupsOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
1 thought / bought / taught · 2 got / chose / wrote · 3 sat / went / had · 4 came / made / ate · 5 flew / took / put · 6 met / said / slept
In other words
“I had a job interview last month.”
“The bus came late, so I took a taxi.”
“I went back home.”
“He told me the news.”
Notice

Notice: these past forms have no -ed. What do they look like?

BasePastExample
gowentI went back home.
havehadI had a job interview.
getgotI got up early.
seesawI saw my shoes.
taketookI took a taxi.
telltoldHe told me the news.
In other words
Many very common verbs are irregular — the past is a new word: go → went, buy → bought.
The form is the same for all persons: I went, she went, they went.
Learn them like new words. Sound groups help: thought / bought / taught · came / made / ate.
Negatives and questions (didn't, Did you…?) come in Lesson 4.

Stage 6 · Practice

Practice

Part 1 — Each sentence has one mistake. Choose the correct sentence.
1❌ “I goed home at ten.”
2❌ “She taked a taxi.”
3❌ “We eated pizza last night.”
4❌ “He telled me a funny story.”
Why

went · took · ate · told — irregular verbs never take -ed.

1Yesterday I ___ TV all evening. (watch)
2I ___ to bed very late. (go)
3She ___ me and we ___ for an hour. (call / chat)
4We ___ a great meal and ___ about the old days. (have / talk)
5He ___ his keys and ___ them under the sofa. (lose → lost / find)
6They ___ at eight and ___ home at midnight. (arrive / leave)
Why

Regular: watched, called, chatted, talked, arrived. Irregular: went, had, lost, found, left.

1❌ “We meeted at the station.”
2❌ “I buyed a new phone.”
3❌ “She finded her keys.”
Why

met · bought · found — irregular verbs never take -ed.

1Last night we ___ a film and ___ pizza. (watch / eat)
2She ___ home and ___ dinner. (come / make)
3I ___ my friend and we ___ for hours. (meet / talk)
4He ___ the shop and ___ some bread. (visit / buy)
Why

Regular: watched, talked, visited. Irregular: ate, came, made, met, bought.

1❌ “We meeted at the station.”
2❌ “I buyed a new phone.”
3❌ “She finded her keys.”
Why

met · bought · found — irregular verbs never take -ed.

1Last night we ___ a film and ___ pizza. (watch / eat)
2She ___ home and ___ dinner. (come / make)
3I ___ my friend and we ___ for hours. (meet / talk)
4He ___ the shop and ___ some bread. (visit / buy)
Why

Regular: watched, talked, visited. Irregular: ate, came, made, met, bought.

Stage 7 · Read

Read

A true story about a very bad morning.
1The story is about…
Why

Everything went wrong — but in the end he got the job.

1He had an interview last month.
2The bus came on time.
3His shoes were two different colours.
4He came to the interview ten minutes late.
5He got the job.
Why

The bus came late. He was forty minutes late — but he got the job.

1The past of “leave” in the story is…
2The past of “see” is…
3The past of “give” is…
4Which word starts the first problem? “___, the bus came late.”
5Which words start the last part? “___, I came forty minutes late.”
Why

left · saw · gave. A story moves with First → Then → After that → In the end.

1Why did he take a taxi?
2What was wrong with his shoes?
3Why was everyone late that day?
4How does the story end?
Why

The bus came late → taxi. Shoes: one black, one brown. The office clock stopped — and he got the job.

1The past of “meet” in the story is…
2The past of “tell” is…
3“___, the bus came late.” Which word is in the story?
Why

met · told. The story moves with First → Then → After that → In the end.

Stage 8 · Listen

Listen

Track 6.18 — the class dinner storyOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
A: …It was my Business Management class dinner on Saturday. B: That's great! How was it? A: I don't know. I didn't go. B: Oh no! Why not? A: Well, first I couldn't find my shoes. I looked everywhere. In the end I used my ordinary shoes. Then the bus was late. I waited for half an hour, but it never arrived! B: Oh no! That's awful! A: I know. After that it started to rain… so I called a taxi. And I waited and I waited… In the end I decided to walk home. I was just so wet by the time I got home. B: What a nightmare! Poor you!
Track 6.19 — reacting to newsOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
Good news: That's brilliant! That's great! That's amazing! Bad news: That's terrible! That's awful! What a nightmare! Oh no! Poor you! Interesting news: Really? That's interesting!
Useful language
  • That's brilliant!
  • That's amazing!
  • That's awful!
  • What a nightmare!
  • Oh no! Poor you!
  • Really? That's interesting!
A student tells a friend about the class dinner… that never happened.

Listen once. Then answer the questions.

1What was the first problem?
2How long did he wait for the bus?
3How did he get home?
Why

First the shoes, then the bus (half an hour), then the rain — in the end he walked home.

1“I passed my exam!” —
2“I waited two hours, and the bus never came.” —
3“I met a famous actor at the airport.” —
Why

Good news → That's brilliant / amazing! Bad news → That's awful! Poor you! Interesting news → Really?

A student tells a friend about the class dinner… that never happened.

Listen once. Then choose True or False.

1The dinner was on Saturday.
2He found his good shoes.
3The taxi arrived quickly.
Why

He used his ordinary shoes, and the taxi never came — he walked home in the rain.

Stage 9 · Write

Write

Write a short true story: a day when everything went wrong.

5–6 sentences. Use First / Then / After that / In the end and at least three irregular verbs.

Useful language
  • First,…
  • Then,…
  • After that,…
  • In the end,…
  • I went / had / got / took…
  • What a day!
Tell your partner a true story: a day when everything went wrong.

Your partner listens and reacts. Then swap.

Useful language
  • First,…
  • Then,…
  • After that,…
  • In the end,…
  • That's awful!
  • Poor you!
Tell your teacher a true story: a day when everything went wrong.

Your teacher listens and reacts. Then swap roles.

Useful language
  • First,…
  • Then,…
  • After that,…
  • In the end,…
  • That's awful!
  • Poor you!
In other words
Step 1 — think for one minute: what happened, in what order?
Step 2 — tell the story with First / Then / After that / In the end. Your partner reacts: “Oh no!”, “What a nightmare!”
Step 3 — swap. Then tell another pair the best story you heard.

Stage 10 · Type it

Type it

Now produce it — type, don’t tap.

Spelling counts. Type the answers, then check.

1He ___ hello to everyone. (say \u2192 past)
2I ___ him at the party. (meet \u2192 past)
3She ___ her keys under the sofa. (find \u2192 past)
Why

Story verbs are irregular: say \u2192 said, meet \u2192 met, find \u2192 found, give \u2192 gave, do \u2192 did.

1He finded his keys.
2She sayed hello.
3I meeted him in 2019.
Why

Story verbs are irregular: say \u2192 said, meet \u2192 met, find \u2192 found, give \u2192 gave, do \u2192 did.

1Rewrite in the past: I give her a book.
2Rewrite in the past: We do our homework.
3Rewrite in the past: They meet at the caf\u00e9.
Why

Story verbs are irregular: say \u2192 said, meet \u2192 met, find \u2192 found, give \u2192 gave, do \u2192 did.
